newsitem.title: CANADA: Alcan plans capex of US$500 mln in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Alcan plans capex of US$500 mln in 1997.

text.p: Alcan Aluminium Ltd plans capital expenditures of US$500 million this year, compared with US$482 million in 1996, president and chief executive officer Jacques Bougie told a news conference on Monday.

Bougie said the company has budgeted about US$400 million for 1997 to "maintain the competitiveness of all our assets," and another US$100 to modernize one of its "pot lines" in the United Kingdom and spend on other small projects.
But Alcan is mulling a number of large investment projects that if realized over the next three years would significantly boost its annual capital expenditure budgets, Bougie said.

Projects requiring an investment decision in 1997 include a new 340,000 to 350,000 metric ton smelter at Alcan's existing facilities in Alma, Quebec, at an estimated cost of about US$1.5 billion, an expansion of its Brazil facilities, and investments in bauxite mining operations.

"We are very prudent in undertaking these projects. Obviously, if we were to go ahead with Alma, and with an expansion in Brazil, and one or two other things, capex would be higher in the years to come," Bougie said.
Alcan is also looking at other potential projects around the world, but does not have definitive plans for them yet.
"There are a number of other projects over the next five years that we would be considering," Bougie said.
He said Alcan would is examining certain investments in Asia for 1997-98, but he declined to discuss details.
"It is a region of very high growth and it is a region in which we have a substantial advantage, having been there since the 1930s, and we intend to capitalize on this opportunity," Bougie said.
One longer-term project is a joint-venture with a China National Non-Ferrous Metals Industry Corp for a 240,000 tonne smelter and thermo-electric facility in Shanxi province, China.
A feasibility study on the previously announced China project will be conducted this year, with a final decision expected in late 1998 or early 1999, Bougie said.
Alcan is also considering several projects that would help reduce the company's dependence on other suppliers of bauxite and alumina, the raw materials needed for aluminum making.

As announced in January, Alcan is considering operating its own bauxite mine in Northern Queensland, Australia, exploiting bauxite reserves it owns there. A feasibility study has been completed and Alcan will make a final decision in the next few months, said Bougie.
"It would be an investment of US$125 million to US$150 million, and the decision will be taken by the end of the year," Bougie said.
If the Australia bauxite project proceeds, mine operations would begin by the end of the decade.
Bougie said all of the investments would be made with regard to the company's financial ability, local costs of production and trends in world aluminum markets.

Looking to western world aluminum production, which increased by an estimated six percent in 1996, Roger Scott-Taggart, Alcan's drector of industry analysis, said about half of 850,000 tonnes of new aluminum smelting capacity coming on stream in 1997-98 will be operational this year.

In addition to the new capacity planned worldwide, industry analysts must also consider the availability of 860,000 tonnes of idled capacity remaining in the 1.6 million tonnes that producers cut back in 1994-96.
Alcan has 160,000 tonnes of idled smelter capacity.
"We will only bring it on stream when world inventories justify it and we have prospects of strong demand ahead of us," Bougie said.
((Reuters Montreal bureau 514-985-2434))
